questionTextHi: If 'P + Q' means 'P is the father of Q' and 'P − Q' means 'P is the wife of Q', then in the expression P + Q − R, how is P related to R?
explanation: P is the father of Q, and Q is the wife of R. So P is the father of R's wife — R's father-in-law.
explanationHi: P is the father of Q, and Q is the wife of R. So P is the father of R's wife — R's father-in-law.

subject: reasoning
questionText: Pointing to a woman, a man said, "Her father is the only son of my father." How is the woman related to the man?
questionTextHi: Pointing to a woman, a man said, "Her father is the only son of my father." How is the woman related to the man?
explanation: The only son of the man's father is the man himself. So the woman's father is the man — she is his daughter.
explanationHi: The only son of the man's father is the man himself. So the woman's father is the man — she is his daughter.

questionTextHi: Introducing a boy, a girl said, "He is the son of my father's only son." How is the boy related to the girl?
explanation: The only son of the girl's father is the girl's brother. The son of her brother is the girl's nephew.

questionText: A man walks 5 km towards north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questionTextHi: A man walks 5 km towards north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point?
explanation: He walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south — the 5 km walks cancel out, leaving 3 km east of the start.
explanationHi: He walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south — the 5 km walks cancel out, leaving 3 km east of the start.

questionText: Ravi walks 10 m towards south, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Which direction is he facing now?
questionTextHi: Ravi walks 10 m towards south, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Which direction is he facing now?
explanation: Facing south, a left turn faces east; another left turn faces north — he is now facing north (10 m east of start).
explanationHi: Facing south, a left turn faces east; another left turn faces north — he is now facing north (10 m east of start).

questionTextHi: In the morning, a person's shadow falls exactly to his right. Which direction is he facing?
explanation: In the morning the shadow falls towards the west. If west is to his right, he must be facing south.

questionText: A person walks 3 km towards east, then 4 km towards north. How far is he from the starting point?
questionTextHi: A person walks 3 km towards east, then 4 km towards north. How far is he from the starting point?
explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.
explanationHi: By Pythagoras theorem: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.

subject: reasoning
questionText: If South-East becomes North and North-East becomes West, and all directions change in the same way, then what will West become?
questionTextHi: If South-East becomes North and North-East becomes West, and all directions change in the same way, then what will West become?
explanation: The whole compass rotates 135° anticlockwise (SE → N). Applying the same rotation, West (270°) → 135° = South-East.
explanationHi: The whole compass rotates 135° anticlockwise (SE → N). Applying the same rotation, West (270°) → 135° = South-East.

subject: reasoning
questionText: A man facing west turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questionTextHi: A man facing west turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
explanation: West + 90° clockwise = North; North − 180° = South. He is facing south.
explanationHi: West + 90° clockwise = North; North − 180° = South. He is facing south.

questionText: K is 40 m to the south of L. M is 30 m to the east of K. What is the shortest distance between L and M?
questionTextHi: K is 40 m to the south of L. M is 30 m to the east of K. What is the shortest distance between L and M?
explanation: The triangle LKM is right-angled at K with legs 40 m and 30 m — distance = √(40² + 30²) = 50 m.
explanationHi: The triangle LKM is right-angled at K with legs 40 m and 30 m — distance = √(40² + 30²) = 50 m.

questionTextHi: If '×' means '÷', '÷' means '−', '+' means '×' and '−' means '+', then find the value of: 9 × 3 ÷ 2 + 4 − 6
